children.cond: Shock, poor perfusion, lethargy or apnea

pill.text: Resuscitate; blood culture, then broad IV antibiotics (meropenem-class) now; INR and glucose; call the hepatology and surgical team now

children.text: Ill-appearing young infant: consider a lumbar puncture, and ask pharmacy for meningitic doses until meningitis is excluded (expert opinion).

pill.text: Check INR and give vitamin K; GI bleeding may be variceal — call hepatology and GI now; then step 2

children.subtext: Go to step 2 — do not wait for a fever to start

children.text: Fever without another source, or shivering
Paler stools
New or deeper jaundice
Abdominal discomfort: vomiting, poor feeding, irritability
Raised WBC, CRP or procalcitonin
Raised or rising ALT/AST
Raised or rising GGT or bilirubin
Bile lakes on ultrasound
BARD Delphi 2022: for first episodes in the first year after the Kasai. Expert consensus, not yet validated prospectively. GGT and bilirubin together count as one B item.

children.cond: 2 from A and 2 from B, or suspected with a positive blood culture

pill.text: Confirmed cholangitis — admit, IV antibiotics 14–21 days
Suspected cholangitis — admit, IV antibiotics 10–14 days

children.cond: Only A, or only B (for example fever with normal labs, or a rising GGT in a well child)

pill.text: Same day: blood culture, labs and ultrasound. BARD sets a very low threshold — if in doubt, treat as suspected cholangitis

children.cond: Fever with a clear other source (otitis, bronchiolitis, UTI, line), normal GGT, bilirubin and stools
children.subtext: Treat that source; recheck bilirubin, GGT and stool color soon. If anything changes, go back to the BARD lists (expert opinion)

children.text: Blood culture before the first dose — 2 sets if you can; culture the line too if there is one.
Start IV antibiotics; do not wait for results. A negative culture does not stop treatment.
Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler at every episode: bile lakes, ascites, portal flow, another source.
Urinalysis and urine culture: UTI is the main alternative source.
INR — vitamin K if prolonged, and before any procedure.
Glucose when feeds stop; restart feeds (NG if needed) as soon as the child is stable.
No society guideline sets the drug. Follow your local antibiogram and ID advice; dose with pharmacy.
Piperacillin–tazobactam is the most common choice (71% of BARD survey respondents); meropenem if local resistance is high.
On prophylaxis: choose a different class from the prophylactic drug.

Avoid ceftriaxone as first choice: it misses enterococci, resistant gram-negatives are common in some series, and it causes biliary sludge that confuses the ultrasound. Contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates (FDA label).
Meropenem-class cover.
Gram-positive cocci in the culture, or no response → add vancomycin.

children.subtext: Narrow to the isolate; keep the full duration

pill.text: Repeat cultures and ultrasound (bile lake, abscess, line); broaden cover; involve hepatology, surgery and ID

children.text: Complete the course: 10–14 days if suspected, 14–21 days if confirmed (BARD Delphi, first year). Give it IV — no data support an early oral switch (lesson 03-07).
Recheck bilirubin after the course. Do not call the Kasai failed until the cholangitis is treated.

children.cond: Single bile lake near the porta

pill.text: Prolonged IV antibiotics; discuss drainage with hepatobiliary surgery and IR in a transplant center

children.cond: Recurrent or hard-to-treat cholangitis, multiple bile lakes, or bilirubin that does not return to its pre-episode level

pill.text: Refer to a transplant center now — recurrent cholangitis is a transplant-referral trigger (expert opinion; lessons 03-07, 03-08, 03-12)
Home with the family plan: pale stools or fever — same day. Review prophylaxis
